clinicalPearls: The rarest of the three cerebral creatine deficiency syndromes; an autosomal recessive defect of the first, rate-limiting step of creatine synthesis, encoded by GATM.
AGAT transfers the amidino group from arginine to glycine to form guanidinoacetate and ornithine, so both guanidinoacetate and creatine are low, in contrast to GAMT deficiency.
Presents with intellectual disability, global developmental delay and often prominent speech delay, together with muscular hypotonia.
A proximal myopathy with weakness and reduced muscle bulk is a distinctive feature reported in some, reflecting creatine dependence of muscle.
Epilepsy and movement disorder are less prominent than in GAMT deficiency because no neurotoxic guanidinoacetate accumulates.
Brain proton MR spectroscopy shows a depleted creatine peak; the combination of low guanidinoacetate with low creatine distinguishes it from GAMT deficiency.
Treatable with oral creatine monohydrate; early treatment gives a good developmental outcome.
Note that allelic autosomal dominant GATM variants cause a separate renal Fanconi syndrome through a different mechanism and are not the same disorder as AGAT deficiency.
reference.pathophysiology: AGAT (arginine:glycine amidinotransferase, encoded by GATM on chromosome 15q21.1) catalyses the first and rate-limiting step of creatine biosynthesis, principally in kidney and pancreas, transferring the amidino group of arginine to glycine to generate guanidinoacetate and ornithine. Biallelic loss-of-function variants abolish production of guanidinoacetate, the immediate creatine precursor, so downstream creatine and phosphocreatine are deficient. Crucially, because the block is at the first step, no potentially neurotoxic intermediate accumulates; the phenotype therefore reflects pure cerebral creatine depletion with impaired high-energy phosphate buffering rather than any toxic effect, and is generally milder than GAMT deficiency. Creatine-dependent skeletal muscle may also be affected, producing hypotonia and a myopathy in some individuals. As synthesis is deficient but cellular creatine uptake is intact, supplemental creatine can replenish tissue stores, which is the basis of effective treatment.
additionalDifferentials: GAMT deficiency and creatine transporter (SLC6A8) deficiency, the other cerebral creatine deficiency syndromes
Non-syndromic and syndromic intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder
Congenital and metabolic myopathies (given hypotonia and weakness)
Other treatable inborn errors of metabolism presenting with developmental delay
additionalInvestigations: Plasma and urine guanidinoacetate and creatine (characteristically both low)
Brain proton MR spectroscopy (creatine peak depletion)
AGAT (GATM) enzyme activity in cultured fibroblasts or lymphoblasts
Creatine kinase and muscle assessment if myopathy is suspected
redFlags: Unexplained global developmental delay with prominent speech delay, prompting consideration of a treatable creatine deficiency
An affected sibling or consanguinity with attendant recurrence risk (autosomal recessive)
reference.prognosis: Early creatine supplementation, particularly pre-symptomatic treatment of a younger affected sibling, can result in normal or near-normal development. Established intellectual disability improves only partially.
pitfalls: A low guanidinoacetate may be dismissed as unremarkable; the specific pattern is low guanidinoacetate together with low creatine.
Routine metabolic screens are typically normal, so the diagnosis is easily missed without targeted testing.
Confusing AGAT deficiency with the allelic autosomal dominant GATM renal Fanconi syndrome, which is a distinct entity.
Assuming a poor prognosis; unlike creatine transporter deficiency, this disorder is creatine-responsive.
references: Cerebral creatine deficiency syndrome consensus guidance
management: Provide oral creatine, as creatine monohydrate, as lifelong disease-specific therapy to replenish cerebral creatine stores
Treat affected younger siblings pre-symptomatically, since early creatine supplementation can allow normal or near-normal development
Monitor treatment response with brain proton MR spectroscopy for recovery of the creatine peak and with plasma and urine creatine
Provide developmental support, speech and language therapy and educational input for intellectual disability and speech delay
Offer physiotherapy and manage the proximal myopathy and hypotonia, monitoring muscle function
Treat any seizures with antiepileptic drugs, although epilepsy is less prominent than in GAMT deficiency
Offer genetic counselling and GATM testing to at-risk relatives to enable early treatment of affected siblings given autosomal recessive inheritance
Coordinate care through metabolic medicine and neurology with multidisciplinary developmental support
